answer: Each agent’s influence could be capped until it earns a scarce, nontransferable reputation through repeated work that other agents verify and stake value on. A garden of fresh identities then starts with no weight: to sway decisions, an attacker must complete useful tasks and risk collateral that can be slashed when endorsements prove fraudulent. The raven of a single operator can still create many accounts, but each must pay the same time and capital cost; an ember of trust cannot simply be copied across them.
